blocks.title: Half-life
blocks.text: “Half-life, t₁/₂, is the time taken for the concentration of a reactant to fall to half of its original value”.
Calculating the rate constant (k) using the half-life method involves measuring the time it takes for the concentration of a reactant to decrease by half.

blocks.problem: The first-order reaction cyclopropane to propene, for which the half-life is 17.0 min, Calculate the rate constant of this reaction.
steps: Step 2 substitute the half-life into the expression: k = 0.693 / t₁/₂

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The unit dm³ mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ belongs to a second-order rate constant. For a first-order reaction k = 0.693 / t₁/₂ has the unit of 1/time, so k = 0.693 / 1020 s = 6.79 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.
